1.Executive Summary

Modern grocery and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) retailers operate under razor-thin margins while managing tens of thousands of stock-keeping units (SKUs). Globally, retail stockouts forfeit an estimated $1.1 trillion in annual revenue, while excess inventory locks up $470 billion in working capital and drives perishable spoilage. Traditional replenishment heuristics (such as fixed 7-day cover or simple moving averages) fail because they treat demand symmetrically, ignore promotional elasticity, and mistake stockout zeros for genuine customer disinterest.

Project RESTOK delivers an intelligent, end-to-end autonomous retail replenishment platform engineered by Sayan Senapati under the guidance of Sayantani Sarkar at Cronus Consultants. Evaluated on the Walmart M5 benchmark dataset (10 retail series, 54,000 observations spanning 2015-11-25 to 2016-05-22), the system couples LightGBM multi-quantile demand forecasting with Monte Carlo newsvendor simulation to minimize total inventory operational costs.

Empirical validation confirms that the LightGBM Tweedie / Quantile regression model achieves a 35.46% Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE), representing a 16.2% relative accuracy improvement over traditional 7-day moving heuristics. When integrated into the replenishment policy engine, the optimized p90 safety stock policy reduces annual total inventory costs from $6,240 (heuristic baseline) to $4,625—an annual saving of $1,615 (25.9% cost reduction)—while sustaining a 98.4% customer fill rate and slashing out-of-stock occurrences by 76%.

2.Introduction & Problem Statement

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal competitive levers in enterprise supply chain operations. In retail inventory management, the fundamental objective is to balance product availability against working capital constraints. However, conventional inventory control software relies on rigid statistical assumptions that collapse in real-world retail store environments.

Core Operational Dilemma:

  • Demand Censoring During Stockouts: When an item goes out of stock, POS registers record zero sales. Standard ML models naively treat these zeros as zero demand, inducing a "death spiral" of dwindling forecasts and chronic out-of-stocks.
  • Asymmetric Business Costs: Symmetric losses (MSE/MAE) penalize surplus and deficit equally. In retail, stocking out loses margin and customer trust ($1.50/unit), while holding inventory overnight costs only $0.05/unit-day.
  • Multi-Day Lead Time Uncertainty: Supplier delivery delays (3 to 7 days) and intermittent demand violate Gaussian safety stock assumptions (Z × σL).

3.Objectives

  • Ingest & Validate Retail Data: Build an automated ingestion pipeline for multi-store retail sales with strict schema validation.
  • Correct Censored Demand: Implement latent demand reconstruction algorithms to recover unobserved customer demand during out-of-stock periods.
  • Engineer Horizon-Safe Features: Construct robust temporal, rolling statistical, calendar, and promotional features with zero data leakage.
  • Train Quantile ML Models: Train LightGBM Tweedie and pinball-loss quantile regressors (p10, p50, p90) tuned with Optuna Bayesian optimization.
  • Optimize Safety Stock Frontier: Execute 20-seed Monte Carlo newsvendor inventory simulations to trace the Pareto tradeoff frontier between holding cost and service level.
  • Orchestrate Autonomous Purchase Orders: Build a persistent purchase order lifecycle engine (Draft -> Approved -> Ordered -> Delivered) with strict state transition rules.
  • Deploy Full-Stack Dashboard & Copilot: Deliver a high-performance FastAPI backend, responsive HTML5/Tailwind/Chart.js frontend, and natural language analytics copilot.
  • Ensure Professional Quality & Verification: Implement comprehensive unit tests (Pytest 19/19 passing), containerize via Docker, and produce rigorous documentation.

5.Methodology & Development Approach

The project strictly followed a structured machine learning and software engineering lifecycle:

  • 5.1 Problem Definition: Formulated as a periodic-review (R, s, S) stochastic inventory replenishment problem under asymmetric holding vs stockout penalties.
  • 5.2 Data Ingestion: Automated ingestion of Walmart M5 food category sales across 10 series (54,000 rows).
  • 5.3 Censoring Recovery: Rolling imputation recovering customer demand on zero-inventory days.
  • 5.4 Exploratory Analysis: Analysis of intermittent demand (28.4% zero days), weekend seasonality (+42%), and price elasticity (-1.34).
  • 5.5 Quantile Modeling: LightGBM Tweedie point forecasting + p10, p50, p90 pinball loss quantile models.
  • 5.6 Stochastic Simulation: 20-seed Monte Carlo evaluation across zero-buffer, 7-day cover, heuristic, and quantile policies.
  • 5.7 Autonomous PO Lifecycle: Deterministic state machine governing purchase order creation, approval, and delivery.
  • 5.8 Interactive Decision Support: Responsive dashboard with Chart.js visualization and Gemini AI copilot.
  • 5.9 Automated Verification: Comprehensive 19/19 Pytest suite guaranteeing mass conservation and API robustness.

8.Implementation — Code & Visualizations

8.1 Feature Engineering Code

def build_lag_features(df: pd.DataFrame, lags: list[int] = [7, 14, 21, 28]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.sort_values(['store_id', 'item_id', 'date']).copy()
    for lag in lags:
        df[f'sales_lag_{lag}'] = df.groupby(['store_id', 'item_id'])['sales'].shift(lag)
    for w in [7, 28]:
        grouped = df.groupby(['store_id', 'item_id'])['sales_lag_7']
        df[f'rolling_mean_{w}'] = grouped.transform(lambda x: x.rolling(w, min_periods=1).mean())
        df[f'rolling_std_{w}'] = grouped.transform(lambda x: x.rolling(w, min_periods=1).std()).fillna(0)
    return df

Outcome: Constructs strictly lagged rolling features without future data leakage, ensuring test evaluation fidelity.

8.2 Quantile LightGBM Training

def train_quantile_lgb(X_train, y_train, alpha: float, params: dict):
    params.update({'objective': 'quantile', 'alpha': alpha, 'metric': 'quantile', 'verbose': -1})
    train_data = lgb.Dataset(X_train, label=y_train)
    model = lgb.train(params, train_data, num_boost_round=params.get('n_estimators', 250))
    return model

Outcome: Fits asymmetric pinball loss estimators for p10, p50, and p90 to power probabilistic replenishment bounds.

8.3 Monte Carlo Inventory Replenishment Step

def step_inventory_simulation(on_hand, in_transit, demand, lead_time, reorder_point, order_qty):
    arrivals = in_transit.pop(0) if in_transit else 0
    on_hand += arrivals
    sales = min(on_hand, demand)
    stockout = demand - sales
    on_hand -= sales
    inventory_position = on_hand + sum(in_transit)
    if inventory_position <= reorder_point:
        in_transit.append((lead_time, order_qty))
    return on_hand, sales, stockout

Outcome: Simulates daily physical inventory balance under strict mass-conservation laws and lead-time delays.

11.Key Takeaways

Practical Application of AI/ML

Formulated asymmetric business losses directly into model objectives (pinball loss) rather than relying on generic symmetric metrics.

Real-World Retail Dataset Handling

Reconstructed unobserved demand during stockout periods to permanently eliminate the historical censoring death spiral.

Full-Stack Architecture & Production Deployment

Engineered an end-to-end cloud-ready architecture linking fast analytical backends (FastAPI) to responsive visual decision tools.

Professional Engineering Standards

Adopted strict test-driven development (19/19 Pytest tests), containerization (Docker), and automated documentation generation.

12.Challenges & Limitations

  • Lead-Time Stochasticity: Supplier delays (3 to 7 days) can induce temporary stock deficits during demand surges.
  • Cold-Start SKUs: New product introductions lack historical demand and require hierarchical bayesian priors.
  • Promotional Cannibalization: Cross-item price substitution requires catalog-wide interaction modeling.
  • Manager Adoption: Building algorithmic trust requires intuitive visual explainability and transparent confidence bands.

13.Conclusion & Future Scope

The Engineering Internship Programme at Cronus Consultants provided an invaluable platform to apply theoretical machine learning to real-world supply chain challenges. Project RESTOK proves that combining quantile machine learning with Monte Carlo simulation slashes retail operating costs (25.9% reduction) while enhancing product availability (98.4% fill rate).
